# Add declaration-vs-behavior verification rules to the core rule set

## Problem Statement

The current priority-rule set demands evidence rigorously for **external**
surfaces — libraries, APIs, vendor behaviour, versions — but has no rule
covering the equivalent failure for **internal** surfaces. An agent can read a
project's own configuration file, assert what it does, design a change around
that assertion, and satisfy every existing evidence rule while being
completely wrong.

This is not hypothetical. It happened three times in a single session on a
production incident, and each instance had to be caught downstream by an
independent validator or a fresh-eyed sub-agent rather than by the agent
holding the context.

The gap has a precise shape:

> Citing a **declaration** is not citing a **behaviour**, but the existing
> rules treat "cited from source" as sufficient evidence.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Trigger

During a spec-driven change in a separate project (`pokeedge`,
`fixPricechartingRefresh`), the orchestrating agent produced three materially
wrong conclusions across the discovery and design gates. All three passed the
agent's own verification standards at the time they were made.

### The three failures, concretely

**Failure 1 — a derived ratio with mismatched populations.**

The agent computed "Chinese cards are being processed roughly 3 times each" by
dividing 12,280 completed work items by 4,225 Chinese cards carrying a provider
ID. The work items actually covered 12,056 **distinct** cards, most of which had
no provider ID at all because they were identity-discovery work, not
price-refresh work. Real rate: 1.01 passes per card. The agent had the data
needed to disprove this and never ran `COUNT(DISTINCT)`.

This conclusion was presented to the user as a finding, and shaped the initial
framing of the change.

**Failure 2 — designing a fix against the wrong mechanism.**

The agent read a priority-scoring YAML file, observed that 30 of 100 available
points were allocated to "data absence" weights, and designed a suppression
mechanism targeting those weights.

An independent validator then read the *producer* that consumes the config and
found two disqualifying facts: one of the two weights was already set to an
empty tuple for the relevant candidate type and therefore contributed zero, and
the actual priority driver was a **fixed band applied before the matrix score
was consulted at all**. The designed suppression would have changed almost
nothing.

The agent had read the config file. It had never read the call site.

**Failure 3 — asserting behaviour from config keys that never matched.**

The same YAML declared `language_bonuses` with keys `en`, `ja`, `jp`, `zh-cn`,
`cn`. The agent reported to the user that English was being deliberately
deprioritised, since English mapped to `0` while other languages received `+4`.

The consuming code read this as
`language_bonuses.get(candidate.language.lower(), 0)`, and the candidate's
language came from a database column holding `ENGLISH`, `JAPANESE`,
`CHINESE_SIMPLIFIED`. Lowercased, those are `english`, `japanese`,
`chinese_simplified` — **matching no declared key**. Every card had silently
scored a zero bonus for the entire life of the feature.

The config was not deprioritising English. The config was dead code. And because
the agent had derived a plausible narrative from it, the false conclusion
propagated into the discovery record and then into a design task built on that
premise.

### Why the existing rules did not catch this

Each relevant rule was either out of scope or technically satisfied.

| Rule | Why it did not fire |
| --- | --- |
| P34 no-unverified-knowledge | Scope is explicitly **external** surfaces: libraries, frameworks, APIs, vendor capabilities. A project's own YAML is not covered. |
| P07 verify | **Technically satisfied.** The agent used tools, read source, and cited file paths. It verified that the config *said* X. It never verified that X *did* anything. |
| P30 docs-before-probing | Concerns ordering when consulting external documentation. Silent on internal declaration-to-effect tracing. |
| P16 docs-first | Directs consulting internal documentation before changing behaviour. The agent did consult internal artifacts — the wrong kind, treated as authoritative. |
| P31 thoroughness | **Satisfied.** The agent ran many production queries, read many files, and spawned validators. Effort was not the failure. |
| P33 structural-correctness | Describes the *fix* for this class of bug once found. Does not direct the agent to look for it during diagnosis. |

The uncomfortable conclusion: the agent performed a **large volume of
well-executed verification aimed at the wrong artifact**. General exhortations
to be thorough cannot catch that, because thoroughness was present. Only a
specific rule naming the failure mode can.

### Why the safety net was too late

Both design-stage failures were eventually caught, by an independent design
validator with fresh eyes and no stake in the prior conclusion. That mechanism
worked exactly as intended.

But it fired **after a complete design had been written on a false premise**,
forcing a full design revision. The cost of catching a wrong mechanism at
design-validation time is an entire discarded draft. The cost of catching it
before drafting is one file read.

## Originally Proposed Direction (now expanded — see Scope Update)

Add two priority rules and one design-gate obligation: P38 declaration-is-not-behavior,
P39 population-identity, and a lever-citation precondition in adv-design.md.

## Scope Update (lite-task expansion)

Initial proposal framed this as "add P38/P39 sections following the existing
P29/P30/P31 pattern." Investigation during proposal-gate discovery surfaced
that the framing was technically correct but misleading:

- **Advance is not the canonical rule source.** No `rules.yaml` exists in the
  advance repo. `~/.config/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml` (user-managed)
  is canonical for the user; SETUP.md only *documents* a subset of recommended
  rules with copy-paste YAML for adoption.
- **Coverage is already drifted.** Of 20 rules deployed in the user's
  `rules.yaml`, only 5 have SETUP.md sections (P29, P30, P31, P33, P36).
  15 deployed rules — including recent additions P32, P34, P35, P37 — have no
  SETUP.md section. P37 broke the documented-adoption precedent silently.
- **No sync enforcement exists.** No CI test, lint, or sync step checks
  SETUP.md ↔ rules.yaml consistency. Drift is structural, not accidental.

Per operator direction, this change expands scope to:

1. **Document P38 + P39 in SETUP.md** (sections following the P29/P30/P31
   pattern). P38 and P39 are already deployed in the user's rules.yaml as of
   this change; SETUP.md now reflects that.
2. **Backfill SETUP.md sections for P32, P34, P35, P37** — the recent
   additions that lack sections. This eliminates the precedent-breaking gap
   and brings documented coverage from 5/20 to 11/22 (P38 + P39 added).
3. **Design-gate lever-citation obligation** in `.opencode/command/adv-design.md`
   — unchanged from original proposal.
4. **CHANGELOG.md entries** for the new sections, matching the existing
   pattern (one bullet per rule section, including backfilled ones).

Rules P04, P05, P07, P08, P16, P19, P23, P24, P25, P26, P27 (the older
"ADV-cited campsite/write-in/locality rules") remain undocumented by name
in SETUP.md. They predate the "ADV recommends rule" documentation pattern
and are out of scope for this change; backfilling them would be a separate
historical-docs change.

## Draft Acceptance Signals

To be firmed at agreement.

- P38, P39, P32, P34, P35, P37 each have a SETUP.md section following the
  established pattern: heading, intro paragraph, copy-paste YAML block,
  priority-calibration rationale, "why this rule exists" prose.
- The design gate contract carries the lever-citation obligation in a form a
  design author can act on and a validator can check.
- Existing documented rules (P29, P30, P31, P33, P36) are not modified unless
  text drift is being corrected; the P30 `scope:` field present in deployed
  rules.yaml but absent from SETUP.md's YAML example may be added for
  consistency.
- CHANGELOG.md gains one bullet per new/backfilled rule section.
- Existing rules are not duplicated or contradicted; P34's external scope and
  P38's internal scope are explicitly distinguished so neither is read as
  superseding the other.

## Constraints

- `rules.yaml` is user-managed. Advance documents and recommends; it must not
  silently write to a user's rule file. (P38 and P39 have already been
  manually adopted by the operator into the deployed rules.yaml as part of
  this change's pre-execution work; that adoption is captured here as
  evidence, not redone by the change.)
- Rule numbering must not collide with existing entries; current set runs to
  P37, this change adds P38 and P39.
- Priority values must be justified relative to neighbours rather than asserted,
  matching how P29, P30 and P31 were introduced.

## Avoidances

- Do not restate P34 with wider scope. The external/internal split is the point;
  merging them loses the specific trigger that makes each actionable.
- Do not add a general "be more careful" rule. The failure occurred while the
  agent was being careful; only a specifically-named failure mode helps.
- Do not make this Python-specific or config-format-specific. The failure mode
  applies to any declaration-to-effect join in any language.
- Do not backfill SETUP.md sections for the older ADV-cited rules (P04-P08,
  P16, P19, P23-P27). They predate the documentation pattern and warrant a
  separate historical-docs change if pursued.

## Evidence Index

- Originating incident: `pokeedge` change `fixPricechartingRefresh`, discovery
  and design gate records, plus four promoted project-level wisdom entries
  covering enum widening, mocked-SQL blindness, activity-versus-outcome
  measurement, and the silent config-default join.
- Existing rule set and priorities: `~/.config/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml`
  (now P04 through P39 after this change's pre-execution adoption of P38/P39).
- Existing adoption pattern for user-managed rules: `SETUP.md` sections for P29
  clean-not-minimal, P30 docs-before-probing, P31 thoroughness.
- Pre-execution adoption: operator manually appended P38 and P39 (YAML folded
  scalar style matching P37) to deployed `rules.yaml` and synced
  `~/toolbox/backups/dotfiles/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml`. YAML strict
  parse remains broken by pre-existing P32 colon-space ("the inverse: run
  them only"); unrelated latent defect, out of scope here.
- Design gate contract: `.opencode/command/adv-design.md`.

# Agreement — addDeclarationBehavior

## Objectives

Document the two newly-deployed rules (P38 declaration-is-not-behavior, P39
population-identity) plus four backfilled recent additions (P32, P34, P35, P37)
in `SETUP.md`, following the established P29/P30/P31 documentation pattern.
Add a lever-citation precondition to the design gate contract. Record the new
and backfilled sections in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1 — Documented rule sections.** `SETUP.md` contains one section per rule
for: P32 (worktree-isolation), P34 (no-unverified-knowledge), P35
(architecture-over-hacks), P37 (no-polling-loops), P38
(declaration-is-not-behavior), P39 (population-identity). Each section follows
the established pattern: heading, intro paragraph framing the agent failure
mode, copy-paste YAML block matching the deployed `rules.yaml` entry,
priority-calibration rationale, "why this rule exists" prose, "Restart OpenCode
after editing" closer.

**AC2 — YAML fidelity.** Each section's copy-paste YAML block matches the
corresponding deployed `rules.yaml` entry verbatim (same `name`, `scope` if
present, `rule` text, `tags`, `hint`, `priority`). Folded-scalar style (`>-`)
is used where the deployed entry uses it (P37, P38, P39) so the YAML remains
strict-parse-safe for those entries.

**AC3 — Ordering.** Sections are added in numeric order. P32 inserts between
the existing P31 section and P33 section. P34 and P35 insert between P33 and
P36. P37 inserts after P36. P38 and P39 append after P37.

**AC4 — Lever-citation obligation.** `.opencode/command/adv-design.md` gains
the "Lever citation" precondition: for every mechanism a design proposes to
change, cite the call site where that mechanism takes effect — not where it is
declared. The obligation is checkable at design drafting, not only by a
downstream validator. The exact text from the proposal is used verbatim.

**AC5 — CHANGELOG entries.** `CHANGELOG.md` gains one bullet per rule section
added or backfilled, following the existing P29/P30/P31 entry style (rule name,
priority, one-line summary of the failure mode it counters, note that
`rules.yaml` stays user-managed).

**AC6 — No regressions.** Existing SETUP.md sections (P29, P30, P31, P33, P36)
are not modified except optionally to add the `scope:` field where the deployed
entry has one and the SETUP.md YAML example lacks it (P30 is the documented
case). Other content is untouched.

**AC7 — No spec deltas, no runtime changes.** No `adv_delta_*` calls. No
changes under `plugin/src/`. No changes to `bin/`. No changes to other
`.opencode/command/adv-*.md` files except `adv-design.md` for AC4.

## Constraints

- **C1 — rules.yaml is user-managed.** This change does not write to
  `~/.config/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml`. The operator has already
  manually adopted P38 and P39 as pre-execution work; that adoption is
  referenced as evidence in the proposal, not redone.
- **C2 — No canonicalization.** This change does not introduce a canonical
  `advance/rules.yaml`, a sync script, or a CI check enforcing SETUP.md ↔
  rules.yaml consistency. That architectural question is explicitly deferred
  to a separate change.
- **C3 — Documented pattern only.** All new SETUP.md sections mirror the
  established P29/P30/P31 shape (heading, intro, YAML block, priority
  rationale, "why this rule exists", restart closer). No new documentation
  format is invented.
- **C4 — Verbatim rule text.** YAML blocks in SETUP.md sections match the
  deployed rules.yaml entries verbatim. The documentation surface must not
  silently diverge from the canonical deployed text.

## Avoidances

- **DONT1 — Don't merge P34 and P38.** The external/internal split is the
  point. Merging them loses the specific trigger that makes each actionable.
- **DONT2 — Don't add a "be more careful" rule.** The failure occurred while
  the agent was being careful; only a specifically-named failure mode helps.
- **DONT3 — Don't make rules language-specific.** The failure modes apply to
  any declaration-to-effect join in any language; examples may reference
  Python patterns but the rule text must stay generic.
- **DONT4 — Don't backfill older ADV-cited rules (P04-P08, P16, P19,
  P23-P27).** They predate the documentation pattern and warrant a separate
  historical-docs change if pursued. Scope creep here would inflate review
  surface without improving correctness.
- **DONT5 — Don't fix the pre-existing P32 YAML strict-parse defect**
  (`"the inverse: run them only"` colon-space). It is a related-scan finding,
  not in scope. Track separately.
- **DONT6 — Don't touch runtime code, specs, or schemas.** Documentation-only
  change.

## Out of Scope

- **OOS1 — Canonicalization architecture.** A canonical `advance/rules.yaml`
  with sync enforcement is a separate architectural change.
- **OOS2 — Older ADV-cited rules documentation.** P04-P08, P16, P19, P23-P27
  SETUP.md sections are out of scope (see DONT4).
- **OOS3 — P32 YAML strict-parse fix.** See DONT5.
- **OOS4 — Adopting the new rules in any downstream user's rules.yaml.** The
  operator's deployed `rules.yaml` already has P38 and P39; other users adopt
  manually per the documented pattern.

# Design — addDeclarationBehavior (lite-task docs-sync)

## Architecture

No new architecture. Documentation-only change touching two surfaces:

| Surface | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Adoption docs | `SETUP.md` | +6 sections (P32, P34, P35, P37, P38, P39), each following the established P29/P30/P31 pattern |
| Design-gate contract | `.opencode/command/adv-design.md` | +Lever-citation precondition |
| Release notes | `CHANGELOG.md` | +6 bullets (one per new/backfilled section) |

## SETUP.md section template (mechanical)

Each new section is structurally identical to P29/P30/P31:

```markdown
## <Rule Name> Rule (P<NN>)

ADV recommends a priority-<N> <one-line description of the rule>. <2-3 sentence
framing of the agent failure mode it counters.>

Like P28-P36, `rules.yaml` is **user-managed** so this change must be applied
manually.

Add the following entry in the `rules:` map (P<NN> recommended):

<yaml block matching deployed rules.yaml entry verbatim>

**Rationale for priority <N>:** parity with <neighbouring rules>. <one-line
calibration vs priority-10 tier boundary>.

**Why this rule exists:** <prose explaining the concrete failure mode and why
general exhortations cannot catch it>.

Restart OpenCode after editing.
```

## Insertion plan (in numeric order)

Current SETUP.md rule-section order: P29 → P30 → P31 → P33 → P36.

After this change: P29 → P30 → P31 → **P32** → P33 → **P34** → **P35** → P36 → **P37** → **P38** → **P39**.

| New section | Insertion point |
|---|---|
| P32 | After P31 section (currently line ~703, before existing P33 at line 707) |
| P34 | After P33 section (currently line ~752, before existing P36 at line 755) |
| P35 | Immediately after P34 |
| P37 | After P36 section (currently line ~793, before "## Project Initialization" at line 797) |
| P38 | Immediately after P37 |
| P39 | Immediately after P38 |

## Per-section source mapping (YAML fidelity)

Each section's copy-paste YAML block is copied verbatim from
`~/.config/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml` after the pre-execution P38/P39
adoption. Source line ranges:

| Rule | rules.yaml source lines (approx) |
|---|---|
| P32 | 173-184 |
| P34 | 202-229 |
| P35 | 231-243 |
| P37 | 257-275 |
| P38 | new (priority 9, declaration-is-not-behavior, scope + rule, `>-` folded) |
| P39 | new (priority 8, population-identity, scope + rule, `>-` folded) |

Folded-scalar style (`>-`) is preserved where the deployed entry uses it (P37,
P38, P39) so the YAML remains strict-parse-safe for those entries. P32, P34,
P35 use plain multiline scalars in the deployed file; their SETUP.md YAML
blocks mirror that.

## Lever-citation obligation — placement

`.opencode/command/adv-design.md` (366 lines). Insertion point: under the
existing methodology section, near the preconditions a design author must
satisfy before validation. The exact text (from proposal, verbatim):

> **Lever citation.** For every mechanism this design proposes to change, cite
> the call site where that mechanism takes effect — not where it is declared. A
> design that cites only a configuration file, constant, or schema declaration
> has not located its lever and is not ready for validation. Where the lever is
> a scoring, ranking, or policy input, additionally confirm no earlier stage
> preempts it (fixed bands, short circuits, hard filters, or empty inputs that
> render the weight inert).

Specific heading/anchor placement TBD at execution time after reading the
file's current section structure.

## Cross-cutting concerns

- **No spec deltas.** Pure documentation. `adv_delta_*` is not invoked.
- **No runtime code.** Nothing under `plugin/src/`, `bin/`, or `scripts/` is
  modified.
- **No worker-bundle impact.** No workflow code touched.
  `adv_change_set_worker_bundle_impact` should classify as `not_applicable`.
- **Cross-route mapping.** Only one route through the docs surface: SETUP.md
  adoption-pattern sections. No conditional/branching behavior across multiple
  locations.

## Verification

- `pnpm run check` will not catch documentation-only changes; primary
  verification is human review of the rendered SETUP.md sections and the
  adv-design.md insertion.
- Optional: `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` against an
  extracted aggregate of the new SETUP.md YAML blocks, to confirm strict-parse
  safety for the new sections specifically. (Pre-existing P32 colon-space
  defect in deployed rules.yaml is out of scope per DONT5.)
- `bin/oc-test smoke` covers format/lint checks if the change touches any
  format-enforced surface.

## Decisions deferred / not made here

- Whether to add a `scope:` field to the existing SETUP.md P30 YAML example
  (deployed has it, SETUP.md doesn't). Left as a same-pattern campsite fix;
  will be applied inline if it fits the diff naturally, otherwise tracked.
- Whether to convert P32's plain scalar to `>-` folded style. Out of scope
  (DONT5).
- Whether to canonicalize advance/rules.yaml. Out of scope (OOS1).

# Executive Summary — addDeclarationBehavior

## Outcome

The Advance rule set now has internal-surface evidence coverage parity with its external-surface coverage. Two new priority rules close the gap that let three confidently-wrong conclusions propagate through a pokeedge production incident, and four previously-undocumented recent additions now have SETUP.md adoption sections matching the established pattern.

## Value / Why It Matters

Before this change, Advance's P34 (no-unverified-knowledge) demanded rigorous evidence for **external** surfaces — libraries, APIs, vendor behavior — but had no equivalent for **internal** surfaces. An agent could read a project's own config file, assert what it does, design a change around that assertion, and pass every existing evidence rule while being completely wrong. The pokeedge `fixPricechartingRefresh` incident proved this three times in one session: dead config keys confidently described as policy, a suppression designed against an inert weight, and a "3 passes per card" ratio derived from mismatched populations.

P38 (declaration-is-not-behavior, priority 9) closes that gap as the internal twin of P34. P39 (population-identity, priority 8) catches the statistics-evidence failure mode. The design-gate lever-citation obligation in `adv-design.md` operationalizes P38 at drafting time, so the gap is caught before validation rather than by a downstream validator.

As a side effect, four previously-undocumented recent rules (P32 worktree-isolation, P34 no-unverified-knowledge, P35 architecture-over-hacks, P37 no-polling-loops) now have SETUP.md sections matching the established P29/P30/P31 adoption pattern. This eliminates the silent precedent-break that began when P37 was added to the deployed rules.yaml without a SETUP.md backfill.

## What Was Built

- **`~/.config/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml`** (pre-execution, operator-applied): P38 and P39 added with folded-scalar style matching P37; backup synced to `~/toolbox/backups/dotfiles/opencode/instructions/rules.yaml`. 20 → 22 rules total.
- **`SETUP.md`**: 6 new sections in numeric order (P32, P34, P35 backfilled; P37, P38, P39 documented). Each follows the established P29/P30/P31 pattern: heading, intro, copy-paste YAML block matching deployed rules.yaml verbatim, priority-calibration rationale, why-this-rule-exists prose. +347 lines, 0 deletions.
- **`.opencode/command/adv-design.md`**: Phase 2 gained a "Lever citation (precondition)" subsection between the ADR rubric and the Keep-the-design-actionable closer, operationalizing P38 at design drafting.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: 7 new bullets under Unreleased > Added (6 rule sections + 1 design-gate obligation).

## Verification

- **YAML fidelity**: machine-verified by adv-verifier — all 6 new SETUP.md YAML blocks character-for-character match deployed rules.yaml entries after 2-space indent normalization (report ID `addDeclarationBehavior|change:verifier:add-declaration-behavior-docs-sync|adv-verification-triage-bundle|1`, status:pass, confidence:high).
- **Section ordering**: P29 → P30 → P31 → P32 → P33 → P34 → P35 → P36 → P37 → P38 → P39 contiguous.
- **No regressions**: `git diff numstat` confirms additions only (adv-design.md 6/0, CHANGELOG.md 7/0, SETUP.md 347/0). Existing P29/P30/P31/P33/P36 sections unchanged.
- **format:check**: `pnpm run format:check` exit 0 (runId `tr_ms2ajbs6`, 17245ms).
- **Contract**: 14 contract items reviewed — 4 constraints respected, 6 avoidances respected, 4 OOS not-applicable. 0 failing rows.

## Risks / Follow-ups

- **P32 latent YAML strict-parse defect** (pre-existing): the deployed `rules.yaml` fails strict YAML parsing at line 179 (`"the inverse: run them only"` colon-space). OpenCode loads instructions as plain text so runtime is unaffected, but any future tooling that machine-parses rules.yaml would choke. Out of scope (DONT5); warrants a separate small fix converting P32 to `>-` folded style.
- **Coverage gap remains**: 9 of 22 deployed rules (P04, P05, P07, P08, P16, P19, P23-P27) still have no SETUP.md section. They predate the documentation pattern. Backfilling them is out of scope (DONT4) and warrants a separate historical-docs change if pursued.
- **No canonicalization**: this change does not introduce `advance/rules.yaml`, sync script, or CI check enforcing SETUP.md ↔ rules.yaml consistency. That architectural question is explicitly deferred (OOS1). Drift between SETUP.md and deployed rules.yaml will continue to be possible unless canonicalization is addressed.
- **Optional P30 campsite fix deferred**: deployed rules.yaml has a `scope:` field on P30 that the SETUP.md YAML example lacks. Adding it would have modified an existing section, which AC6 prohibits. Deferred.

## Originating Incident Recap

This change originated as a cross-project follow-up from the pokeedge change `fixPricechartingRefresh`. Three concrete failures during discovery and design gates demonstrated the gap:

1. A "3 passes per card" ratio (12,280 work items / 4,225 cards with provider IDs) was actually 1.01 passes per distinct card — the work items covered 12,056 distinct cards, most without provider IDs. → P39.
2. A suppression designed against priority-scoring weights that were already empty tuples or preempted by a fixed band applied before the matrix score. → P38.
3. A claim that English cards were being deliberately deprioritized, when the `language_bonuses` config keys matched no runtime value (candidate languages came from a database column with different naming). → P38.

The full RCA with the three failures, the table of why each existing rule did not catch them, and the proposal-direction rationale lives in the proposal artifact.
